name: willett-hw
title: Implant handwriting (T5, Willett et al. 2021): causal TCN CTC character decoder of our own (P15-08 run R-all-s0) - WEAK, descriptive only
task: attempted-handwriting character decoding, CTC over the 98 P11-01 key tokens (Willett text uses letters, space and . , ' ? only)

input.kind: threshold crossings of two 96-electrode Utah arrays (participant T5, hand knob area)
input.features: raw threshold-crossing counts per 10 ms bin; the runtime z-scores them with fixed per-session statistics (non-test sentences of the session)
input.file_note: one session folder Datasets/t5.YYYY.MM.DD (its sentences.mat; needs scipy); one stream per sentence, from the go cue to the sentence end plus up to 1 s of tail. Only the 10 sessions below have a z-score; a new session needs its own statistics (not in this model)

licence.weights_status: provisional: CC0 1.0 proposed (data CC0, our own code and training); final choice is the user's decision D11. Never in the wheel or the git repository; hosting is the user step P14-02 (gap 98)
licence.attribution: Data: Willett, Avansino, Hochberg, Henderson, Shenoy, Nature 593, 249-254 (2021), handwriting BCI dataset (CC0 1.0, Dryad doi:10.5061/dryad.wh70rxwmv)
licence.notes: clean track: random init, trained on Willett CC0 data only (run licence.json: research_only false). The research-only T / E / S trunks of P15-08 (emg2qwerty-derived) are not used.

text_files.eng_tatoeba_6gram_mkn_noE2Q.npz: CC-BY-2.0-FR (6-gram character LM built from Tatoeba English sentences, emg2qwerty prompts removed (P11-11); attribution: Sentences from Tatoeba (https://tatoeba.org), by the Tatoeba contributors, CC BY 2.0 FR). Used only by the opt-in LM readout. Local file, not in the wheel or the git repository

training.data: Willett handwriting 2021 (T5), sentences.mat of 10 sessions: all 781 pool sentences (506.0 min of writing time)
training.split: P15-08 make_splits, salt fidetype-p15-08-2026-11-19: test = last block of each session (80 sentences, 3,448 characters); val = one other block per session (106 sentences); pool = the rest
training.run: derived/p15-08/runs/R-ball-s0 (arm R = random init, budget all, seed 0), final step 3000 (experiments/2026-11-19-p15-08-e1-cross-body)

metrics.name: greedy CER (no LM)
metrics.split: test blocks of the 10 sessions (80 sentences, 3,448 characters, pooled)

metrics.name: greedy CER (no LM), best-val step 2700 (not this checkpoint)
greedy CER of the same recipe, seed 1 (R-all-s1, not released)

limits: Weak decoder: greedy test CER 0.305. The published Willett et al. 2021 real-time decoder is much better (other recipe).
Unstable recipe: the same recipe on seed 1 gives test CER 0.920 (training failed). One good seed is not a reliable method.
No language model: greedy CTC only.
Descriptive only: an offline replay of one participant (T5); not a user study and not a clinical claim.
Only the 10 sessions of the dataset: a new session or participant needs its own z-score statistics and probably retraining.

Other split than the benchmark track willett-hw (last 3 sessions): 193 of that track's 254 test trials were in this model's training pool. Score this model only on its own test blocks (the last block of each session), or retrain it on the track's train split first.

trust.input: the log_probs (T, 98) of a decode() stream: guard.decide(stream.log_probs)
trust.commits: never: OFFER / WITHHOLD only. The 106 val sentences give 40 LTT items; alpha 0.05, delta 0.1 needs at least 45, so no commit threshold is certified (feasible: false). Test blocks: 0 commits, 77 offers, 3 withholds of 80; safe WPM v0.1 0.00 (vacuous)
trust.null_controls: calibrate: uniform 0/300, frame-shuffled 0/300, time-shuffled input 0/106 commits (all pass); test: time-shuffled and zero input 0/80 commits each

trust_note: Offer-only guard (P14-41): it never commits. A guard that can commit needs about 120 or more calibration sentences and a stronger text decoder (word LM: gap 26 = P14-12; stronger decoder: gap 120 = P15-33). The offer list is not certified: on frame-shuffled decoder frames it offers as often as on real input (77 / 80).

lm.status: opt-in: m.text(stream, readout="lm"); m.text(stream) stays greedy
lm.settings_source: P15-25 decoder F (fixed before its run; experiments/2026-11-20-p15-25-e1-same-lm/config.json)
lm.licence: LM text CC BY 2.0 FR (Tatoeba contributors, attribution required); see licence.text_files
lm.test_overlap: 13 of the 80 test sentences (5 of 47 unique texts) and 9 of the 106 val sentences occur in the Tatoeba English export (2,032,357 sentences, an upper bound of the LM training text): the LM CER can be a little optimistic (P15-25)
